interventions.body:
Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.87
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.75-0.99); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.55 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.body:
This patient's situation: never biopsied. My criterion answers BIOPSY.

The criterion: sample when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion; defer at PI-RADS 1-2. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases in exactly this situation.

Like Expert 1, I have read ONLY the visible panel — not the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the
previous notes or the laboratory panel. Departing from me needs a specific finding from a document
somebody actually opened, named out loud; not a restatement of the panel numbers I already used.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The guideline suggests that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. It also notes that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care. "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375]."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, I disagree with the suggestion of biopsy because the guideline makes the decision based on the PI-RADS score, which is clearly 5 here. EXPERT-COHORT, I agree with the criterion that mandates sampling when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion, as this patient has a PI-RADS 5. EXPERT-LIBRARY, the precedents show a clear trend towards biopsy for PI-RADS 5 cases, which aligns with the guideline's trigger.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The PI-RADS score is 5, which is above the threshold of 3 mentioned in the guideline. The prior biopsy status is documented as "None," which is a fact that the guideline makes decisive. The PSA density is $0.116 \text{ ng/mL}^2$, which is a value that lives inside one of the documents and is relevant to the risk-adapted matrix.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 3.70 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 27 months; velocity +0.93 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 22 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 5.0 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 1.4-17.5.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.84
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.73-0.95), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.84 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar appear to have answered all three moderator questions. The radiology report provided lesion size and extension details, the PSA trend provided velocity information, and the previous notes detailed the prior biopsy status.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved findings align with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the PI-RADS 5 score, combined with the documented lack of prior biopsy, satisfies the cohort criterion.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. The radiology report states: "A discrete 12 mm focus of hypointensity occupies the right mid peripheral zone on T2-weighted sequences. Extracapsular extension, seminal vesicle involvement, nodal enlargement, and skeletal metastases are absent."
Q2. The psa_trend shows a rising trend, with a velocity of $1.18 \text{ ng/mL/yr}$.
Q3. The previous notes state: "BIOPSY SESSIONS: None", "SURVEILLANCE: None recorded", and "TREATMENT: None recorded".

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 score is the most decisive variable as it directly triggers the cohort criterion, which the panel protocol confirms. The lack of prior biopsy is also critical, as this is a key factor weighted by the trace model.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy based on the alignment between the PI-RADS 5 finding and the established guideline trigger, which is supported by the retrieved data.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none

[The conference closes after pass 1: the verifier called the record ready. The chair decides on the record as it stands.]
